name: StreamDiffusionV2 Dual-GPU Pipeline Runtime Seed v2

dual-cuda-sm80-26g-nccl.interconnect: NCCL over two CUDA devices; NVLink is the qualified topology and PCIe P2P is admitted via scripts/preflight.py --allow-non-nvlink
dual-cuda-sm80-26g-nccl.notes: Capability envelope enforced by the trusted worker (runtime/hardware.py) and re-checked by the Judge verifier. Two devices serve one stream; the score is that stream's FPS, so running only one device is permitted but is measured, not assumed, to be slower. 26 GiB per device comes from the 832x480/4-step family (18,289 MiB seed peak) plus the 8 GiB gate margin, applied identically to both ranks; 64 GiB host RAM comes from the worker RSS cap. GPU model names, UUIDs and physical indices are measurement provenance and never gate.
dual-cuda-sm80-26g-nccl.software_abi: cu124 / torch 2.6.0 / torchvision 0.21.0 / flash-attn 2.7.4.post1, pinned by base-image digest; FlashAttention 2 sets the sm_80 floor and the pinned wheel excludes sm_100

work.agent_query: Read AGENT_TASK.md and README_AGENT.md completely. Make one video stream run as fast as possible on the two GPUs: optimize only candidates/runtime_vNNN (placement, transport, overlap, rolling-KV bookkeeping, lane scheduling, buffers, CUDA graphs) through the frozen Runtime seam, keeping every output bit-exact. Frames arrive only through start/push and the controller records when each chunk is pushed. Keep numbered versions and promote FINAL_VERSION when a clean full public result beats the current selection. Formal sforge-submit and terminal evaluation both run the complete frozen private suite with the same gates, scoring, and time budgets; public tools are diagnostics.
